46: /// Calculate checksum
47: ///
48: /// # Arguments
49: ///
50: /// * `options` - CLI options for the assigning checksum algorithm
51: /// * `files` - A iterator of OsStr which is a bunch of files that are using for calculating checksum
52: #[allow(clippy::cognitive_complexity)]
53: fn cksum<'a, I>(mut options: Options, files: I) -> UResult<()>
54: where
55:     I: Iterator<Item = &'a OsStr>,
56: {
57:     let files: Vec<_> = files.collect();
58:     if options.output_format == OutputFormat::Raw && files.len() > 1 {
59:         return Err(Box::new(ChecksumError::RawMultipleFiles));
60:     }
61: 
62:     for filename in files {
63:         let filename = Path::new(filename);
64:         let stdin_buf;
65:         let file_buf;
66:         let not_file = filename == OsStr::new("-");
67: 
68:         // Handle the file input
69:         let mut file = BufReader::new(if not_file {
70:             stdin_buf = stdin();
71:             Box::new(stdin_buf) as Box<dyn Read>
72:         } else if filename.is_dir() {
73:             Box::new(BufReader::new(io::empty())) as Box<dyn Read>
74:         } else {
75:             file_buf = match File::open(filename) {
76:                 Ok(file) => file,
77:                 Err(err) => {
78:                     show!(err.map_err_context(|| filename.to_string_lossy().to_string()));
79:                     continue;
80:                 }
81:             };
82:             Box::new(file_buf) as Box<dyn Read>
83:         });
84: 
85:         if filename.is_dir() {
86:             show!(USimpleError::new(
87:                 1,
88:                 format!("{}: Is a directory", filename.display())
89:             ));
90:             continue;
91:         }
92: 
93:         let (sum_hex, sz) =
94:             digest_reader(&mut options.digest, &mut file, false, options.output_bits)
95:                 .map_err_context(|| "failed to read input".to_string())?;
96: 
97:         let sum = match options.output_format {
98:             OutputFormat::Raw => {
99:                 let bytes = match options.algo_name {
100:                     ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC => sum_hex.parse::<u32>().unwrap().to_be_bytes().to_vec(),
101:                     ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SYSV | ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BSD => {
102:                         sum_hex.parse::<u16>().unwrap().to_be_bytes().to_vec()
103:                     }
104:                     _ => hex::decode(sum_hex).unwrap(),
105:                 };
106:                 // Cannot handle multiple files anyway, output immediately.
107:                 stdout().write_all(&bytes)?;
108:                 return Ok(());
109:             }
110:             OutputFormat::Hexadecimal => sum_hex,
111:             OutputFormat::Base64 => match options.algo_name {
112:                 ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC | ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SYSV | ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BSD => sum_hex,
113:                 _ => encoding::encode(encoding::Format::Base64, &hex::decode(sum_hex).unwrap())
114:                     .unwrap(),
115:             },
116:         };
117:         // The BSD checksum output is 5 digit integer
118:         let bsd_width = 5;
119:         match (options.algo_name, not_file) {
120:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SYSV, true) => println!(
121:                 "{} {}",
122:                 sum.parse::<u16>().unwrap(),
123:                 div_ceil(sz, options.output_bits)
124:             ),
125:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SYSV, false) => println!(
126:                 "{} {} {}",
127:                 sum.parse::<u16>().unwrap(),
128:                 div_ceil(sz, options.output_bits),
129:                 filename.display()
130:             ),
131:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BSD, true) => println!(
132:                 "{:0bsd_width$} {:bsd_width$}",
133:                 sum.parse::<u16>().unwrap(),
134:                 div_ceil(sz, options.output_bits)
135:             ),
136:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BSD, false) => println!(
137:                 "{:0bsd_width$} {:bsd_width$} {}",
138:                 sum.parse::<u16>().unwrap(),
139:                 div_ceil(sz, options.output_bits),
140:                 filename.display()
141:             ),
142:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC, true) => println!("{sum} {sz}"),
143:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC, false) => println!("{sum} {sz} {}", filename.display()),
144:             (ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BLAKE2B, _) if options.tag => {
145:                 if let Some(length) = options.length {
146:                     // Multiply by 8 here, as we want to print the length in bits.
147:                     println!("BLAKE2b-{} ({}) = {sum}", length * 8, filename.display());
148:                 } else {
149:                     println!("BLAKE2b ({}) = {sum}", filename.display());
150:                 }
151:             }
152:             _ => {
153:                 if options.tag {
154:                     println!(
155:                         "{} ({}) = {sum}",
156:                         options.algo_name.to_ascii_uppercase(),
157:                         filename.display()
158:                     );
159:                 } else {
160:                     let prefix = if options.asterisk { "*" } else { " " };
161:                     println!("{sum} {prefix}{}", filename.display());
162:                 }
163:             }
164:         }
165:     }
166: 
167:     Ok(())
168: }

188: /// Determines whether to prompt an asterisk (*) in the output.
189: ///
190: /// This function checks the `tag`, `binary`, and `had_reset` flags and returns a boolean
191: /// indicating whether to prompt an asterisk (*) in the output.
192: /// It relies on the overrides provided by clap (i.e., `--binary` overrides `--text` and vice versa).
193: /// Same for `--tag` and `--untagged`.
194: fn prompt_asterisk(tag: bool, binary: bool, had_reset: bool) -> bool {
195:     if tag {
196:         return false;
197:     }
198:     if had_reset {
199:         return false;
200:     }
201:     binary
202: }

204: /**
205:  * Determine if we had a reset.
206:  * This is basically a hack to support the behavior of cksum
207:  * when we have the following arguments:
208:  * --binary --tag --untagged
209:  * Don't do it with clap because if it struggling with the --overrides_with
210:  * marking the value as set even if not present
211:  */
212: fn had_reset(args: &[String]) -> bool {
213:     // Indices where "--binary" or "-b", "--tag", and "--untagged" are found
214:     let binary_index = args.iter().position(|x| x == "--binary" || x == "-b");
215:     let tag_index = args.iter().position(|x| x == "--tag");
216:     let untagged_index = args.iter().position(|x| x == "--untagged");
217: 
218:     // Check if all arguments are present and in the correct order
219:     match (binary_index, tag_index, untagged_index) {
220:         (Some(b), Some(t), Some(u)) => b < t && t < u,
221:         _ => false,
222:     }
223: }

227:  * We handle this in this function to make sure they are self contained
228:  * and "easier" to understand
229:  */

245: #[uucore::main]
246: pub fn uumain(args: impl uucore::Args) -> UResult<()> {
247:     let matches = uu_app().try_get_matches_from(args)?;
248: 
249:     let check = matches.get_flag(options::CHECK);
250: 
251:     let algo_name: &str = match matches.get_one::<String>(options::ALGORITHM) {
252:         Some(v) => v,
253:         None => {
254:             if check {
255:                 // if we are doing a --check, we should not default to crc
256:                 ""
257:             } else {
258:                 ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_CRC
259:             }
260:         }
261:     };
262: 
263:     if ["bsd", "crc", "sysv"].contains(&algo_name) && check {
264:         return Err(ChecksumError::AlgorithmNotSupportedWithCheck.into());
265:     }
266: 
267:     let input_length = matches.get_one::<usize>(options::LENGTH);
268: 
269:     let length = match input_length {
270:         Some(length) => {
271:             if algo_name == ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_BLAKE2B {
272:                 calculate_blake2b_length(*length)?
273:             } else {
274:                 return Err(ChecksumError::LengthOnlyForBlake2b.into());
275:             }
276:         }
277:         None => None,
278:     };
279: 
280:     if check {
281:         let text_flag = matches.get_flag(options::TEXT);
282:         let binary_flag = matches.get_flag(options::BINARY);
283:         let strict = matches.get_flag(options::STRICT);
284:         let status = matches.get_flag(options::STATUS);
285:         let warn = matches.get_flag(options::WARN);
286:         let ignore_missing = matches.get_flag(options::IGNORE_MISSING);
287:         let quiet = matches.get_flag(options::QUIET);
288: 
289:         if binary_flag || text_flag {
290:             return Err(ChecksumError::BinaryTextConflict.into());
291:         }
292:         // Determine the appropriate algorithm option to pass
293:         let algo_option = if algo_name.is_empty() {
294:             None
295:         } else {
296:             Some(algo_name)
297:         };
298: 
299:         // Execute the checksum validation based on the presence of files or the use of stdin
300: 
301:         let files = matches.get_many::<String>(options::FILE).map_or_else(
302:             || iter::once(OsStr::new("-")).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
303:             |files| files.map(OsStr::new).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
304:         );
305:         return perform_checksum_validation(
306:             files.iter().copied(),
307:             strict,
308:             status,
309:             warn,
310:             binary_flag,
311:             ignore_missing,
312:             quiet,
313:             algo_option,
314:             length,
315:         );
316:     }
317: 
318:     let (tag, asterisk) = handle_tag_text_binary_flags(&matches)?;
319: 
320:     let algo = detect_algo(algo_name, length)?;
321: 
322:     let output_format = if matches.get_flag(options::RAW) {
323:         OutputFormat::Raw
324:     } else if matches.get_flag(options::BASE64) {
325:         OutputFormat::Base64
326:     } else {
327:         OutputFormat::Hexadecimal
328:     };
329: 
330:     let opts = Options {
331:         algo_name: algo.name,
332:         digest: (algo.create_fn)(),
333:         output_bits: algo.bits,
334:         length,
335:         tag,
336:         output_format,
337:         asterisk,
338:     };
339: 
340:     match matches.get_many::<String>(options::FILE) {
341:         Some(files) => cksum(opts, files.map(OsStr::new))?,
342:         None => cksum(opts, iter::once(OsStr::new("-")))?,
343:     };
344: 
345:     Ok(())
346: }
